analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia, 29 October 2026
key_insights: US equities rose on Wednesday: S&P 500 +0.28%, Nasdaq +0.27%, Dow +0.19%, Russell 2000 +0.41%. Breadth was slightly negative. The AI and momentum trade outperformed for a second day, led by semiconductors and memory on strong chip earnings and Oracle's analyst day.
Treasuries were mostly weaker with the curve steepening and long-end yields up 5-6 bp. WTI crude settled up 2.9%, back above $100 a barrel, on reports of likely US military action after the midterms.

The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% with two dissents (Cook and Hammack) in favor of a 25 bp hike. Chair Warsh gave no forward guidance. The statement upgraded activity to expanding at a strong pace and kept inflation as elevated. Market pricing implies about an 85% chance of a December hike.

The Fed dropped September's language that the hike would support a timelier return of inflation to 2%. It now says more information will help determine the appropriate stance. Early analyst reactions called the statement largely as expected with a slightly hawkish lean.

Warsh said the FOMC will change its schedule from next fall while keeping eight meetings a year. One 2027 meeting will focus on strategy with no rate vote or statement, and six policy-setting meetings are expected in 2028.

Media reports say the US told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after next week's midterms. The US is moving an extra Patriot battery to Israel and preparing bombers. Trump has not decided but is leaning toward an attack. Qatar and Pakistan are mediating a draft with a 7-day confidence-building timeline.

Oracle's investor day projected $30B of free cash flow in the fiscal year ending May 2029 versus consensus of -$7.3B, and $225B of FY30 revenue (35% CAGR). It plans to self-fund growth from FY29 and limit extra funding to $20B over FY27-FY30, split equally between equity and debt. Neoclouds including Coreweave rallied in sympathy.

The AI trade bounce is attributed to financing announcements: Meta's nearly $100B raise, SpaceX's $40B GPU deal and Broadcom's $63B custom-chip SPV. Anthropic's S-1 keeps the November IPO timeline intact and shows $650B+ in compute commitments. Semiconductors rose about 6.5% and memory about 7.5% over Monday and Tuesday.
Goldman Sachs noted hedge fund net exposure is among the lowest of the year, with the largest two-week institutional tech liquidations on record.

Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday after the close and Amazon on Thursday, with a combined $600B of projected annual AI capex under scrutiny. Consensus cloud growth is about 89% y/y for Google Cloud, 44% for Azure and 39% for AWS. Some previews see Google Cloud beating and Azure re-accelerating. Meta sold off last week on aggressive spending plans despite strong revenue.

US sector moves: energy, money-centre banks, credit cards, investment banks and restaurants outperformed. Software, regional banks, insurers, online brokers, transports, homebuilders, staples, media and telecom lagged. PCE inflation and the first Q3 GDP estimate are due Thursday.

Large US earnings reactions: Vertiv +16.5% on a beat and raised guidance, Oracle +10.6%, F5 -20.4% on weak billings and deferred revenue, Enphase -16.0% on weak residential solar demand, CoStar -14.0% after net new bookings fell 56% y/y, Lennox -10.6% on a 10% guidance cut.

Wendy's rose 15.2% after confirming a $1.4B take-private offer from Trian at $7.35 a share, about a 20% premium to Tuesday's close but a 2.5% discount to the 12-Aug close. LCI Industries rose 8.6% on an unsolicited $101 a share cash proposal from Monomoy, while PATK reaffirmed its June merger agreement with LCII.

European equities were mostly higher in narrow trade: DAX +0.4%, FTSE 100 +0.1%, CAC unchanged. Bund yields rose 2 bp to 3.37% while gilt yields fell about 2 bp after the UK Budget. Guidance quality mattered more than headline beats, with raised targets rewarded at Standard Chartered, Deutsche Bank and ASM International and cuts punished at Adyen and Sandoz.

The UK Budget was low-key. The OBR cut fiscal headroom to £15B from £24B, cut 2027 GDP growth to 1.0% from 1.6% and raised net borrowing forecasts by £65B. The bank surcharge is 3% over 15 months, less than feared, and online gambling VAT rises to 25%. The UK 10-year yield fell about 3 bp to just above 5.30%. DMO 2026-27 gilt issuance is planned at £250.6B versus £249.6B expected.

The FT expects the BoE to start a short, precautionary tightening cycle in November, in line with a Reuters poll majority for a 25 bp hike to 4%. Markets price up to four hikes next year. Chief Economist Pill noted the current inflation shock differs from 2022-23, with a weaker labor market and consumption.

European gas stays near multi-year highs, with Dutch TTF near its highest since December 2022 and storage at about 74.9%. Persian Gulf LNG exports averaged about 30% of normal in October and QatarEnergy cargoes to Italy will not resume until end-December. Goldman sees upside risks to the winter TTF outlook.

Europe shows a rotation from AI enablers to defensives. Morgan Stanley says European AI enablers have lagged MSCI Europe by 25% since the June peak and banks are down 12% from their August high, while medtech, life sciences, pharma and tobacco are up 14%. Bank of America is negative on the Stoxx 600, Rothschild and UBS are constructive on earnings.

Asia: the Kospi closed up 6.63%, Nikkei +1.08%, Shanghai Composite +0.72%, Hang Seng +0.23%. SK Hynix's Q3 and shareholder return plan lifted markets. Investors stayed cautious ahead of Friday's BOJ meeting.

SK Hynix Q3 operating profit of KRW83.3T beat consensus of KRW77.5T. It signed long-term agreements with 14 customers covering over 50% of 2027-28 capacity, expects the memory supply gap to last through 2030, announced a KRW20T buyback and KRW14T dividend and expects significantly higher FY27 capex.

The RBNZ held its OCR at 2.75% against a 25 bp hike expected, in a 4-3 vote, and said further increases are likely. The 2Y yield fell more than 10 bp and the NZ dollar fell over 1% to a two-week low. Australian September CPI came in hotter and lifted November RBA hike odds to almost 80% from 70%.

China is expected to issue at least CNY2.2T of net government bonds in the last two months of the year, the second-largest on record for the period, with November possibly the peak. The MOF said CNY550B of remaining local government bond quotas will be fully issued by year-end.

Reliance's Jio Platforms listed in India's biggest IPO and rose about 21%, valuing it near INR12.5T ($131.5B) and making it the second-largest Indian company by market cap. The IPO was over 22 times oversubscribed. Indian equities still closed lower.

market_movers.rationale: Norsk Hydro was placed on negative catalyst watch at JPMorgan ahead of the 25-Nov CMD. The broker warned costly spot LNG for Alunorte could drive further 2027 consensus downgrades, cut 2027 EBITDA 9% and lowered its target.
Ryanair was downgraded to neutral at Oddo. Limited FY2028 fuel hedging raises cost exposure and competition and price-sensitive demand constrain fares, prompting a 17% profit forecast cut.
Remy Cointreau was downgraded to Sell at TP ICAP Midcap, which argued the recovery was priced in after substantial gains and that China shipment timing flattered cognac.

sector_views.rationale: Morgan Stanley notes the basket has underperformed MSCI Europe by 25% since the June peak while defensives such as medtech, pharma and tobacco are up 14%.
Bank of America projects about 10% further downside by Q2 2027 and Citi flagged rising bearish bets. Rothschild and UBS are more constructive on earnings growth.

earnings_insights: Vertiv Q3 reported: large earnings and revenue beat, organic growth well ahead of consensus, Q4 guidance above the Street and FY guidance raised. Shares +16.5%.
Oracle investor day (guidance, not a print): FY29 free cash flow target $30B versus consensus -$7.3B, FY30 revenue $225B. Shares +10.6%.
SK Hynix Q3 reported: operating profit KRW83.3T versus KRW77.5T consensus, operating margin about 80%, DRAM prices up high-20% q/q. Operating profit beat by about 8%.

GE Vernova Q3 reported: EPS, revenue and EBITDA beat, orders +96% organically, FY26 revenue, margin and FCF guidance raised, buyback authorization doubled to $20B, $9B Trench Group acquisition agreed. Shares -1.9%.
Robinhood Q3 reported: EPS and revenue missed but EBITA ahead of consensus. Funded customers and ARPU were light, total platform assets ahead. Shares -3.3%.
Boston Scientific Q3 reported: revenue better, earnings in line, operating margin missed. Q4 and FY guidance cut, citing an August cybersecurity incident and softer Endoscopy. Shares -5.8%.
Lennox Q3 reported: EPS missed consensus by 7% and FY guidance was lowered by 10% on Residential HVAC weakness. Shares -10.6%.
CoStar Q3 reported: revenue and EPS beat and FY26 guidance raised, but net new bookings fell 56% y/y and missed consensus sharply. Shares -14.0%.
Enphase Q3 reported: results missed on weaker US and France residential solar demand, Q4 revenue guide below consensus, FCF negative. Shares -16.0%.
F5 FQ4 reported: earnings and revenue better, operating margin a touch light, billings and deferred revenue below consensus. FY27 guide above the Street, extra $1.5B buyback. Shares -20.4%.
Etsy reported: EBITDA, revenue and GMS beat, core marketplace GMS +9%, active buyers up y/y for the first time in two years, FY26 outlook raised. CFO to depart in early 2027. Shares +5.4%.
Stellantis quarterly adjusted EBIT reported at €256M versus €191M expected. Cash burn of €4B was below the €4.5B analyst estimate. Shares +15.4%.

Deutsche Bank Q3 profit reported ahead of expectations, revenue guidance improved to above €33B. Standard Chartered raised guidance to operating income growth above 7% from 5%-7% and RoTE above 14% from above 12%.
UBS Q3 net profit reported broadly in line, but underlying pre-tax profit missed after ten consecutive consensus beats. Cumulative savings target raised to $13.7B. Shares -0.6%.

Kone quarterly adjusted EBIT reported at €369M versus €376.1M consensus. Symrise guided margin to the lower half of its 21.5%-22.5% range despite 5.3% organic sales growth versus 5% consensus. Shares -10.2%.
Sandoz quarterly sales missed expectations and annual sales growth outlook was reduced. Shares -2.7%.

Hyperscaler previews (estimates, not prints): consensus cloud growth is about 89% y/y at Google Cloud, 44% at Azure and 39% at AWS. Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday after the close, Amazon on Thursday.

Alibaba won a court injunction against US defense department contract restrictions.
